sections.html:
Gulfport is a port city on the Mississippi Sound in Harrison County, and it is one of the county's two seats. The 2020 count was 72,926 residents. The city covers 64.2 square miles, of which 56.9 are land, with Interstate 10 across the middle, U.S. 90 along the coast and U.S. 49 ending in town from the north.

Annexation drew the map. Gulfport took in the older settlements of Mississippi City and Handsboro in 1965, and in December 1993 it added 33 square miles to the north, including the historic community of Turkey Creek. A house can therefore sit near the beach, along a bayou or in a newer northern subdivision, and each setting brings its own insurance, flood and repair questions. Which school district a house falls into, Gulfport or Harrison County, depends on the address, so confirm it before you tell a buyer.

For land records, Harrison County has two judicial districts. The Chancery Clerk's first district office for recording and redemption is at 1801 23rd Avenue in Gulfport.

sections.h2: Hurricane history and the age of the houses
sections.html:
Two hurricanes reset the building stock. Camille in August 1969 pushed 21 feet of storm water into the waterfront areas and nearly destroyed the port. Katrina in August 2005 brought winds of at least 100 miles per hour and a surge of at least 19 feet, and 9,571 houses in the city were damaged or destroyed.

Many homes standing today were rebuilt or repaired after 2005. If you own one, find out what work was permitted, who did it and whether the paperwork is in a drawer. Buyers and their lenders will ask the same things.

Humid heat and frequent rain wear on a Gulfport house, and tropical storms are the main severe weather risk. Four things get the most attention:

  • Roof coverings, flashing and vents after wind events.
  • Air conditioning systems that run most of the year.
  • Wood trim, siding and crawl spaces where moisture collects.
  • Windows and doors that must seal against driven rain.

An owner who has put this work off may find a traditional sale stalls at inspection. That is one reason some Gulfport sellers look at an as-is cash sale instead.

The city checks properties against state law, city ordinances and zoning rules, and it says it prefers voluntary compliance. Complaints arrive through the 311 system, by phone at (228) 868-5718, or from staff who spot problems on their rounds. An officer typically visits within 24 hours to see whether a violation exists.

Gulfport applies the International Property Maintenance Code with a local amendment adopted as Ordinance 2812. Inspectors look at the outside of the property. They need your signed consent to enter, or a court warrant if access is denied and necessary.

After a notice, the city's FAQ describes your options:

  • Ask the inspector named on your compliance letter for more time. Extensions are routinely granted for hiring a contractor or special circumstances.
  • Meet the inspector on site to go over the violation, and contest charges at a council hearing before the hearing or court date.
  • If violations stay unresolved, the city can issue a citation or correct the problem itself through the City Council process, which may lead to fines or a lien on the property.

A lien from city cleanup has to be dealt with at or before closing. Read any notice you have received and keep your response in writing.

Harrison County bills real property taxes on December 1, and they are due by February 1 without interest. Interest of one half percent per month starts February 2. The county accepts payments until the Friday before its tax sale on the last Monday of August.

The bill is true value times assessment ratio times millage rate. Class I covers a single-family home lived in by its owner and uses 10 percent of true value, while Class II covers everything else at 15 percent. Every parcel must be revalued by the assessor at least once in four years.

The county's land redemption page warns that paying back taxes on a property does not make you its owner, and that a property sold at tax sale stays with the owner until the redemption period ends. If you are behind, the sale should account for the balance. Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and who qualify for homestead can exempt the first $75,000 of true value. Look at your record to see whether that is on file.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a house in Gulfport
sections.html:
Three routes are open to you, an agent listing, a sale on your own or a cash offer, and they run at very different speeds. Sections 89-1-501 through 89-1-523 of the Mississippi Code require a seller of covered residential property to hand the buyer a written statement of the property's condition, early enough to matter before title passes. Ask your agent or attorney whether your sale falls under those sections.

The deed is recorded with the Harrison County Chancery Clerk, and a title search usually comes before closing. Outstanding liens, unpaid taxes and heirs who never signed off are the most common reasons a Gulfport closing slips.

A practical order of work: pull your deed and any mortgage statement, get the tax balance from the Harrison County Tax Collector, ask the city whether any code notice is open on the address, and gather permit and repair records, especially anything done after 2005. With those four items in hand, any buyer, agent or investor can give you a clear answer faster.

A cash sale to an investor can skip showings, listing repairs and lender appraisal delays. In return, the offer has the buyer's repair costs built in. Set it beside the net from a listing after commissions and repairs. We do not promise a price here, and an offer is only an offer until you sign.

faqs.q: Is Gulfport the county seat of Harrison County?
faqs.a: Yes, Gulfport is one of two county seats. Harrison County moved its seat to Gulfport in 1902, and the Chancery Clerk keeps land records in both Gulfport and Biloxi.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Gulfport?
faqs.a: By February 1 each year without interest. Bills go out from Harrison County on December 1, and interest at 0.5 percent a month starts on February 2.

faqs.q: Can a house in Gulfport be sold with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. Open violations and city cleanup liens generally get resolved, disclosed or paid from your proceeds at closing, so find out from the code office what is still open. Inspectors will generally discuss an extension if you contact the officer on your notice.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the Harrison County tax sale deadline?
faqs.a: The property is listed for the tax sale on the last Monday of August and offered to registered tax purchasers. You stay the legal owner during the two-year redemption period, but you must pay the taxes, interest and fees to redeem.

faqs.q: Does hurricane damage history affect selling in Gulfport?
faqs.a: It can. Katrina damaged or destroyed 9,571 houses in the city, so buyers and insurers often ask about past repairs, elevation and permits. Gather any records you have before listing or asking for a cash offer.
